newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania army gets back stolen missiles.
newsitem.headline: Albania army gets back stolen missiles.

text.p: Albania's Defence Ministry said on Thursday it had recovered 16 long-range battlefield missiles stolen last month from a southern garrison near the Greek border.
Thieves had snatched the surface-to-surface and surface-to-air missiles, bought from China in 1995 for $10 million, from a base near the village of Arshi Lengo, 230 km (150 miles) south of Tirana.
"The missiles, found in cooperation with criminal police, are safe at a military depot," said Pandeli Ristani, defence ministry spokesman.
He declined to give further details.

Military sources said the missiles were stolen along with the beds on which they rested, their ignition mechanism, their target-locating mechanism and an instruction manual. It was unclear whether the thieves knew how to use them.
"We are extremely relieved now that the stolen missiles are back in a safe place -- not in Gjirokaster," said Colonel Gligor Koroveshi, an army commander in Gjirokaster.
The looting of the missiles was by far the most serious theft from Albania's demoralised military.
The armed forces almost completely dissolved last March in the face of widespread civil unrest that followed the collapse of pyramid investment schemes.

A British defence expert, Paul Beaver of Jane's Information Group, said the surface-to-surface missiles were almost certainly the land-based version of the Silkworm, which has a range of around 70 km (45 miles) and has been exported by China to a number of countries.

An estimated one million weapons are in private hands in Albania after armouries were broken open in March. The Socialist-led Albanian government is preparing a draft law to be sent to parliament for the collection of weapons.
